subject: FastShop integration — SDK handoff, endpoint migration and rate-fence checklist

Thanks for the intro last week. We want to get the integration runway set up this month — main asks from our side are:
- a quick SDK starter (Python + Node) with auth examples and a simple generation + embeddings sample
- recommended retry/timeouts and rate-fence guidance we can apply on the client side
- an endpoint migration plan: we need to move traffic from our existing gateway to Redwood without disruption (blue/green or staged cutover)

I've attached a quick mutual action plan with milestones. Can you confirm who on your side will take the implementation lead and an estimated timeline for a sandbox cutover? Also need sandbox API keys (non-prod) and a sample rate-limit header layout we can parse.

Hi Elena — great to meet you. Looping in Monica (CSM) and Vivek (integration lead). High-level plan below, attaching a small SDK sample bundle and the quickstart doc.

Proposed handoff & timeline:
1) This week: exchange sandbox keys + MAP sign-off (LAUNCH week 0)
2) Week 1: SDK drop (Python/Node) + sample app to validate auth and a round-trip generation + embeddings call
3) Week 2: Endpoint migration dry-run (staged traffic, 10%/50%/100% window) with Canary period (48h)
4) Week 3: Production cutover and monitoring handover

Client-side guardrails (short):
- Timeouts: request timeout = 8s for API call, token streaming client keepalive = 30s
- Retries: idempotent requests (embeddings) -> up to 3 retries, non-idempotent (generation) -> prefer client-side dedupe + server-side idempotency tokens
- Backoff: exponential backoff 200ms initial, multiplier 2, max 5s + full jitter
- Rate-limit headers we emit: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch sec)

Quick SDK snippets (for the sandbox README):
- Python (requests):
```
import requests
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer <SANDBOX_KEY>", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
payload = {"model":"open-qa-7b", "input":"Summarize this order"}
r = requests.post("https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate", json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=8)
print(r.json())
```
- Node (fetch):
```
const res = await fetch("https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate", {method: 'POST', headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer '+KEY}, body: JSON.stringify(payload), timeout: 8000});
const body = await res.json();
```

Attachments included: integration_samples.zip (small apps + tests) and redwood-sdks-quickstart.md. Monica will coordinate the MAP sign-off. Vivek — can you confirm the server-side policies (rate fences, fallback) and recommended canary windows?

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sdks-quickstart.md (md)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Elena Garcia <elena@fastshop.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-22T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastShop -> Redwood: integration kickoff & SDK samples request

Thanks — quick technical notes and defaults we recommend for FastShop's workload. TL;DR: keep client-side timeouts conservative, use idempotency for retries where possible, and parse the rate headers for soft-fail behavior.

Retries/timeouts (recommended):
- Generation calls: client timeout 8-12s. Server will stream tokens; for streaming clients use a 30s keepalive connection. Retry only on network errors or 5xx; do not retry on 4xx.
- Embeddings: safe to retry up to 3 times with idempotency token. Cache embedding vectors for 7 days to reduce load.
- Backoff policy: initial 250ms, multiplier 2, max 6s, full jitter. Use jitter to avoid thundering herd.

Rate-fence guidance:
- We emit standard headers. We also support a tenant-level header X-Client-Tier that maps to different burst budgets. For FastShop start with tier=standard and set a per-minute soft-limit of 60 requests/min with a 120s refill window for burst smoothing.
- If X-RateLimit-Remaining <= 5 trigger client-side degraded UX flow (queued background flush).

Endpoint migration (technical):
- Provide a sandbox domain (sandbox.fastshop.redwood.example) and a staging domain (staging.fastshop.redwood.example). Use a weighted DNS or gateway route to shift 10%/50%/100%.
- DNS TTL: set to 30s during migration.
- Fallback: keep previous endpoint in the client config as fallback_url. Use header X-Redwood-Variant for diagnostics.

Observability:
- Instruments to add on your side: request id (x-request-id), latency histogram, and the X-RateLimit-Remaining metric. We'll share a pre-built Grafana dashboard link after MAP sign-off.

Small retry helper (JS) we recommend (to include in samples):
```
async function retryWithJitter(fn, attempts=3) {
  let base = 250;
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn(); } catch(e) {
      if (i===attempts-1) throw e;
      let wait = Math.min(6000, base * Math.pow(2,i));
      // full jitter
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.random()*wait));
    }
  }
}
```

Canary window suggestion: 48h at 50% with automatic rollback if error rate > 2% or P50 latency > 2x baseline.

I'll upload the dashboard link and sample Prometheus queries to the Drive referenced in the MAP.

— Vivek (Integration Lead)
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick addition from the runtime/ops playbook perspective — endpoint migration checklist and monitoring play: 

Pre-cutover (dry run):
- Provision sandbox and staging keys, install SDKs, run smoke tests (auth + a 1k token generation + embeddings sanity)
- Configure logging: x-request-id, client tier headers, and sampling at 1% for full traces
- Create a canary alert in Console: error rate > 1% over 5m or latency P95 > 3s

Cutover steps (blue/green):
1) Shift 10% traffic to Redwood staging domain for 2h. Verify success criteria (no errors, stable CPU/GPU utilization).
2) Shift 50% for 48h with synthetic traffic runs.
3) 100% cutover and keep enhanced observability for 7 days.
4) Rollback: switch DNS to previous endpoint and revoke staging keys if we hit rollback triggers.

Traffic shaping & throttles:
- Use token bucket smoothing: allow burst up to 3x nominal for short windows (30s) then apply the soft limit.
- Client should respect Retry-After header on 429s. If missing, exponential retry with jitter and a max of 3 attempts.

Operational runbook snippets to include in the handoff doc:
- Post-cutover checks: 1) errors <= baseline + 0.5% 2) P50 latency within 1.5x baseline 3) token consumption within expected range
- If elevated model latency observed, switch to a smaller model variant (open-qa-3b) automatically via routing policy for non-critical paths.

Attaching the integration_samples.zip which includes a small smoke test harness and CI step that runs on PRs. Please confirm sandbox key rotation cadence (we recommend rotating after cutover).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: integration_samples.zip (zip)]
